title: Sports Follow · Health
description: Is it working for fans? Reachability from outside, alerts firing, each fan journey's success rate, sign-in, and whether live scores, pushes, the Feed and player pages are fresh. Open it first: deploy/RUNBOOK.md says what to look for.

panels.title: Reachable from outside
panels.description: Share of Grafana's uptime checks (Mumbai and Singapore, each minute) that got a healthy answer from /api/health over the range: DNS, the certificate, Caddy and the API together. Under 100%: the Synthetics page says which probe and why.

panels.title: API answers without a server error
panels.description: Share of API requests over the range not answered with a 5xx (health checks and live streams aren't counted). Few requests make this jumpy: read it with the count beside it.

panels.title: Server errors (5xx)
panels.description: API requests answered with a server error over the range. Each is on the API dashboard's Failed requests, with its trace.

panels.title: Errors logged
panels.description: Exceptions logged by the API and worker, and errors the web app reported, over the range. The Errors dashboard groups them by what failed and where.

panels.title: Alerts firing now
panels.description: The Sports Follow folder's alert rules (deploy/grafana/rules.json and app-rules.json) that are firing or about to. The runbook says what each means and what to do.

panels.title: Fans' journeys over the range
panels.description: Each thing fans do, by the API routes it calls (the runbook lists them): its requests, how many were answered with a server error (5xx) or refused (4xx: a wrong code, a missing page), and the share answered without a server error.

panels.title: Codes sent
panels.description: Sign-in codes emailed over the range (POST /api/auth/email/start answered 200; a second tap within the minute counts again).

panels.title: Signed in
panels.description: Codes that signed a fan in (POST /api/auth/email/verify answered 200).

panels.title: Codes used
panels.description: Sign-ins by code for each code sent, over the range. Low: codes aren't arriving (Resend, the spam folder) or fans give up. Few sign-ins make it jumpy.

panels.title: Wrong codes
panels.description: Codes refused at sign-in (verify answered 400: wrong, run out, or not 6 digits).

panels.title: Code limits hit
panels.description: Sign-in requests refused with 429: an address or network asked for too many codes or tried too many wrong ones, or the day's codes ran out (fans read "has sent all the sign-in codes it can today").

panels.title: Send failed
panels.description: email/start answered 502 (Resend refused or didn't answer) or 503 (email isn't set up on the server). Fans can't sign in by email while this grows.

panels.title: Sign-in requests, by step and answer
panels.description: Each interval of the chart: start = a code asked for, verify = a code tried, google/start and google/callback = Continue with Google (the callback always answers 303: its failures are in the API's warnings).

panels.title: Games behind
panels.description: Live games not polled for three of their rounds (at least 3 minutes), now: their scores and alerts are late. The Jobs and live polls dashboard shows why.

panels.title: Oldest score
panels.description: How old the live score is on the live card that's furthest behind, now.

panels.title: Not pushed
panels.description: Moments found over 3 minutes ago that nobody has pushed yet, now. Over 0: fans aren't getting alerts.

panels.title: Delivered
panels.description: Share of pushes over the range that their push service took (unsubscribed devices, 404 and 410, are left out). The Notifications dashboard has the failures by push service.

panels.title: Feed, 24 h
panels.description: New videos about followed players the curator kept in the last day, whatever the range. 0 for a day: the Feed is going stale, and the Feed dashboard shows where its funnel stops.

panels.title: Cards failed
panels.description: Player pages (cards) whose build failed, now: fans see an error on them. The Jobs and live polls dashboard has the builds; the worker's warnings say why.
